messages.subject: Deducer documentation for beginners
messages.subject_clean: Deducer documentation for beginners
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

In the process of switching to R in my computer science course, I found that there is not much online documentation for the beginner. So, I wrote up the following pdf documentation that you may find useful. Even though some of the documentation is specific to the particular statistical tests for my course much of it is general.

Setup for R <http://www.cslab.pepperdine.edu/warford/cosc320/cosc-320-Setup-for-R.pdf>

Data management in R <http://www.cslab.pepperdine.edu/warford/cosc320/cosc-320-Data-management-in-R.pdf>

Curve fitting in R <http://www.cslab.pepperdine.edu/warford/cosc320/cosc-320-Curve-fitting-in-R.pdf>

Plotting basics in R <http://www.cslab.pepperdine.edu/warford/cosc320/cosc-320-Plotting-basics-in-R.pdf>

Plotting curve fits in R <http://www.cslab.pepperdine.edu/warford/cosc320/cosc-320-Plotting-basics-in-R.pdf>

Learning how to use R can be frustrating because, although it is simple after you learn how to use it, it is not intuitive. Furthermore, practically all the online documentation, manuals, and YouTube videos are presented from the perspective of someone who knows the R command line, assumes the user knows the R command line, and/or explains how to use Deducer in terms of the R command line.

This perspective of the common documentation is not helpful, either to the undergraduate student who is learning both the software and the statistics behind it or to the undergraduate professor who has an aversion to the command line and is considering switching to R.

Deducer is a fantastic tool and is no doubt responsible for much of the increase in the use of R in the academic community. I think, however, that a bottleneck in the path to future growth is the command-line-centric perspective of most of the documentation for Deducer.

Best regards,
Stan

J. Stanley Warford
Computer Science Department
Pepperdine University
Malibu, CA 90263

Yes, same issue here, after the two java security updates, one released by Apple the other by Oracle
I am on Mac Os 10.8.4, R 3.01, JGR 1-15, deducer 0.7-6

I found a preliminary fix. Downloading the current JDK as a dmg from Oracle restored the responsiveness of the menu and brought back the full functionality of the buttons.
Please be careful, when selecting the downloadable java versions, the complete JDK 7 is required, JRE is not sufficient.
When I open JGR by double clicking on the JGR icon, it displays an RJavaClassLoader instead of JGR.
That is still a bit strange, but at least I am back in business and able to continue to work with deducer until somebody comes up with a better solution.

Wouldn't like be without deducer, which is a great GUI and has become an indispensable tool to me when working with R. I really appreciate what Ian Fellows has done here for the R community.
Many thanks to Ian.

Rudolf

messages.subject: JGR, Deducer and Java on Mountain Lion
messages.subject_clean: JGR, Deducer and Java on Mountain Lion
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mac Users

I am describing a convenient solution that permits continued use of the Apple's previous java with certain programs such as JGR, while at the same time having the new JDK supplied by Oracle set as the default java engine for general use.

Java has become a bit more tricky on a Mac lately. The reason being that Oracle has taken over maintenance and distribution of newer java versions starting with 1.7, while Apple is still responsible for the previous version 1.6 on the mac.

That means the actual java version that is running on a mac may vary depending on the OS X and which updates from Apple or Oracle have been applied. I am talking about Mountain Lion (10.8.4) here. There is also a difference between java runtime engine (JRE) and java developer kit (JDK).

The default java that is running on a system can be checked via terminal by simply typing java -version.

Apple's and Oracle's java versions differ in some aspects and reside at different locations on the Macintosh HD. Apple's java can be found in System/Library/ Java/JavaVirtualMachines, whereas Oracle's java is in /Library/ Java/JavaVirtualMachines.

While the java preference panel makes it easy to switch among different Oracle versions, switching between Oracle and Apple java is not that easy anymore, since Apple has removed a former control panel where the order of the preferred java engine could be changed.

In my experience, when Oracle java JDK 1.7 (jdk-7u25-macosx-x64.dmg) has been installed as the default java engine, JGR 1.7-15 will start, but it fails to properly display its icon on the left side of the menu, being replaced by "RJavaLoader". Deducer does appear to function normally though.

When running with Apple's older java 1.6 (java version "1.6.0_51", Build …M4509), both JGR and Deducer load and work as usual.

I was looking for a solution to keep and use both java versions on my mac, the new more secure Oracle version 1.7 as default java for general use, and, if required, Apple's old java to resort to for specific use only, for instance with JGR.

Turns out that is not too difficult to do.

Obviously, I did not want to keep changing things around each time before starting JGR.

Instead, I created a simple app that does the job. This was done as follows,

Open AppleScriptEditor

type in the following 3 lines

do shell script "JAVA_HOME=/System/Library/Frameworks/JavaVM.framework/Versions/1.6.0/Home

export JAVA_HOME

/Applications/JGR.app/Contents/MacOS/JGR"

save the app

by selecting  "Application" from the drop down menu  and name the app e.g. JGR-run

The script assumes that both java 1.6 and JGR.app 1.7-15 are found at their typical locations on the mac.

If that is not the case the path needs to be changed accordingly.

Double clicking the new JGR-run.app will invoke the java version specified in the script and start JGR.

In contrast, double clicking the JGR.app will start JGR under the default java environment.

Please note that this solution serves the purpose of using the current JGR.app with the old java supplied by Apple while running by default Oracle's newer java.

Here's more specific information in hopes that it'll help in providing an answer:

I have two data sets: 1) "train", and 2) "test"

I am trying to predict the likelihood of survival for individual passengers on the Titanic based on a few variables (age, sex, and passenger class)

When I create the model I use the following:

model.glm <- glm(forumula=survived==1 ~ pclass + age + sex,family=binomial(),data=train,na.action=na.omit)

I can then output the predictions by using the following:

tmp <- predict(model.glm,type="response")
train[names(tmp),"predicted")<-tmp

So far so good. Now, however, I want to apply the model to my "test" data set. Here is where I run into trouble.

tmpTest <- predict(model.glm, type="response")
test[names(tmpTest),"predicted")<-tmpTest

When I write that code, it looks like the predictions are fine BUT I actually get the same predictions in the same order as I did with the "train" data set even though the "test" data set is completely different. So while I'm trying to apply the model to the "test" data set and ouput predictions to that set, instead it looks like I'm just applying the model to the "train" data set again and outputing the predictions for "train" to "test"

What am I doing wrong?

messages.body_plain:
Kevin,

You should just be able to double click on the jgr executable now to open jgr. Regarding Java, the launcher has a problem when there is a missmatch between 32/64 bit java and 32/64 bit R, so I recommend having both installed.

Manuel,

I'll contact you off list when I get a new launcher ready for testing. In the mean time to help you, and to help me in debugging, can you try the following.

1. make sure you have java installed.
2. open R in c:\Program Files\R\R-3.0.1\bin\i386\Rgui.exe and run:
install.packages(c("rJava","iplots","JGR","Deducer","JavaGD"))
.libPaths()
library(JGR)
launchJGR <- function(){
	windows <- .Platform$OS.type == "windows"
	ws <- function(s){
		if(windows) gsub("/","\\\\",s) else s
	}
	ps <- if(windows) ";" else ":"
	qs <- function(s){
		paste0("\"" , s , "\"")
	}
	rhome <- ws(R.home())
	libs <- ws(paste(.libPaths(),collapse=ps))
	libUser <- ws(Sys.getenv("R_LIBS_USER"))
	arch <- sessionInfo()$R.version$arch
	rJavaPath <- ws(path.package("rJava"))
	jriJarPath <- ws(paste0(path.package("rJava") , "/jri/JRI.jar"))
	jgrJarPath <- ws(paste0(path.package("JGR") , "/java/JGR.jar"))
	iplotsJarPath <- ws(paste0(path.package("iplots") , "/java/iplots.jar"))
	boot <- ws(paste0(rJavaPath,"/java/boot"))
	javaHome <- J("java.lang.System")$getProperty("java.home")
	java <- ws(paste0(javaHome,"/bin/java.exe"))
	path <- J("java.lang.System")$getProperty("java.library.path")

	cp <- paste(qs(jriJarPath), qs(iplotsJarPath), qs(jgrJarPath),
		qs(paste0(rhome , ws("/etc/classes"))),
		qs(paste0(rhome , ws("/etc/classes/classes.jar"))),sep=ps)

	Sys.setenv(PATH=path)
	Sys.setenv(R_HOME=rhome)
	Sys.setenv(R_ARCH=arch)
	Sys.setenv(R_LIBS=libs)
	Sys.setenv(R_LIBS_USER=libUser)
	cmd <- paste0(qs(java), " -Xmx512m ", " -cp ", qs(boot),
	" -Drjava.class.path=", cp,
	" -Drjava.path=",qs(rJavaPath),
	" -Dmain.class=org.rosuda.JGR.JGR "," -Djgr.load.pkgs=yes ",
	" -Djgr.loader.ver=1.7", " -Dr.arch=",arch,
	" RJavaClassLoader")
	system(cmd,wait=FALSE)
	cmd
}
launchJGR()

3. If that doesn't work, open R in c:\Program Files\R\R-3.0.1\bin\x64\Rgui.exe and run the same code.

Send me the full output (i.e. copy the whole R session) off list to i...@fellstat.com.

best,
Ian
